## Overview

**Scope:** original English base game, main rulebook **v1.2**, base glossary, official base FAQ and official base Icon Overview. Marine Worlds and optional solo mode are excluded.

In Ark Nova you plan and build a modern, scientifically managed zoo. You build enclosures according to the animals' way of life and support conservation projects to ensure the preservation of animal species. Gathering diverse animals increases the attractiveness of your zoo, advancing you on the **Appeal track** and generating higher revenues; careful stewardship lets you support conservation projects, advancing you on the **Conservation track** with corresponding bonuses. These two tracks progress in **opposite directions**. If your counters meet or cross at the end of your own turn or during a break, final turns begin. Whoever achieves the best combination of appeal and conservation has built the most successful zoo and wins.

Association work in different zoo associations allows you to partner with zoos and universities around the world; together with specialists and sponsors, they help you manage the tasks needed to achieve your goals.

Ark Nova does not play in formal rounds: players simply take turns (clockwise), one turn at a time, until the end of the game is triggered. In between there are **breaks** — administration phases in which you discard down to your hand limit, recall workers, and gain income. On your turn you always perform one action using one of the 5 Action cards displayed below your zoo map; the position (card slot) of the Action card determines how much you can do with that action.

## Components

**Cards**
- 212 Zoo cards: 128 Animal cards, 64 Sponsor cards, 20 Conservation Project cards
- 12 Base Conservation Project cards
- 11 Final Scoring cards
- 20 double-sided Action cards (5 per set: Build, Cards, Animals, Association, Sponsors — each with side I and side II)

**Tiles & tokens**
- 90 standard enclosures in various sizes (1–5 spaces; both sides of a given size are the same shape — occupied side vs. empty side showing the size number)
- 12 special enclosures: 4× Petting Zoo, 4× Reptile House, 4× Large Bird Aviary
- 34 kiosk / pavilion tiles (kiosk and pavilion are opposite sides of the same tile)
- 20 partner zoos, 12 universities, 15 unique buildings
- 9 Bonus tiles
- 70 money tokens, 20 X-tokens
- 8 Venom tokens, 8 Constriction tokens, 8 Multiplier tokens
- 1 Break token

**Boards & mats**
- 1 game board (Zoo card deck and 6-card display, Reputation track, Appeal track, Conservation track, Break track, Bonus spaces)
- 1 Association board
- 8 player mats (zoo maps): 4× Map A (map for first-time players with a starting advantage — easy), 4× Map 0 (more bonus spaces — intermediate), and Maps 1–8 on the reverse sides (advanced, each with an individual special ability)

**Per player color** (black, blue, red, yellow): 3 counters (appeal, conservation, reputation), 25 player tokens, 4 association workers

**Other:** 2 organizers (general supply), 1 glossary, 1 icon overview, rulebook

## Setup

**Global setup**
1. Place the game board in the center. Place the **Break token** on the start space of the Break track corresponding to your player count (e.g., with three players, the space marked 3).
2. Shuffle the 9 **Bonus tiles** and place a random tile face up on each of the **4 blank yellow spaces beside the Conservation track: two beside 5 conservation and two beside 8 conservation**. Do not place tiles on the two yellow spaces with icons. Return the remaining 5 tiles to the box (unused).
3. Shuffle the **Zoo cards** into a face-down deck on its board space. Deal 6 face-down cards to the display spaces on the board.
4. Place the 2 organizers next to the board as the general supply.
5. Place the **Association board** next to the game board, leaving room for one row of cards above and one row below.
   - 5a. Place 1 partner zoo of each continent and 1 university of each kind on the spaces provided on the Association board.
   - 5b. Shuffle the **Base Conservation Project cards** and keep them face down next to the board. In a 4-player game place the 4 topmost face up below the board; otherwise the 3 topmost.
   - 5c. **2-player game only:** take 6 player tokens of an unused color and cover: on the face-up Base Conservation Project cards, the left level on the left card, the middle level on the middle card, and the right level on the right card; and on the Association board, the three spaces in the left column of the donation area. Covered levels/spaces are blocked and cannot be used by either player.
6. Shuffle the **Final Scoring cards** and place them face down next to the Association board.
7. Randomly determine a start player. Turn order is clockwise.

**Personal setup (each player)**
- **A.** Take a random Map A zoo map and place it that side up (recommended for the first game; all Map A copies are identical). Map 0 suits beginners after the first game. Maps 1–8 (reverse sides) are advanced maps, each with an individual special ability: with these, take 2 random zoo maps and choose 1 of the advanced maps — or lay out player count +1 advanced maps and choose 1 each in reverse order of play. Return unselected maps to the box. Map A's ability (same for all players): at the beginning of the game, place an empty 3-space enclosure **and a kiosk** on the indicated spaces. The printed kiosk already counts as built; place a kiosk tile over it as a reminder. You may build adjacent to it.
- **B.** Take one set of Action cards (Build, Cards, Animals, Association, Sponsors). Place one card **side I up** under each of the five card slots on your zoo map: the **Animals** card under the leftmost slot (showing 1), the remaining 4 randomly under the other slots.
- **C.** Choose a color and take all its components.
  - **C1.** Place your appeal, conservation, and reputation counters on the first spaces of their tracks. On the **Appeal track**, stagger by turn order: start player on space 0, second player on space 1, third on space 2, fourth on space 3.
  - **C2.** Place 7 player tokens on the designated spaces at the left edge of your zoo map; keep the rest next to your map for later use.
  - **C3.** Place 1 association worker on the notepad of your zoo map (the active worker) and the remaining 3 lying down on the designated spaces below the notepad.
- **D.** Take 25 money and put it on your notepad.
- **E.** Draw 2 Final Scoring cards and place them next to your zoo map. You may look at them at any time, but keep them hidden from other players.
- **F.** Draw 8 Zoo cards; keep 4 as hand cards and discard the other 4 to a face-up discard pile on the board. Keep hand cards hidden. (Tip from the rulebook: choose 1–2 Sponsor and 2–3 Animal cards without conditions you cannot fulfill early, ideally matching the Base Conservation Projects on display.)
- **G.** After everyone has chosen their hand cards, reveal the 6 cards of the display.

**Map A bonuses:** its seven support-token bonuses, from top to bottom, are snap one display card, build a size-2 standard enclosure free, gain five money, gain one conservation, gain two reputation, gain twelve money and gain three X-tokens. The first four are received immediately when uncovered and again as break income; the last three are one-time. Take a chosen bonus before or after its project's reward. On Map A the second partner zoo upgrades a card, the third hires a worker and the fourth grants two conservation. The second university upgrades a card and the third grants two conservation. Other maps use their printed bonuses.

**University tiles:** your hand limit is **three cards without the hand-limit university, five cards with it**, checked only at breaks. Other universities do not raise or lower that limit.

| University | Research icons | Reputation on acquisition | Hand-limit effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Research university | 2 | 0 | No change; normally 3 |
| Research/reputation university | 1 | 2 | No change; normally 3 |
| Hand-limit university | 0 | 1 | Raises 3 to **5** |

Take printed reputation when acquiring the university. **Only its research icons count as zoo icons; its reputation award and hand-limit symbol are benefits, not additional zoo icons.**

**Your zoo map:** buildings go in the large central area. You may not build on rock and water spaces (some animals need an enclosure next to rock or water). A built-on space is "covered." Spaces with a special icon may not be built on until you upgrade your Build Action card. Some spaces show a **placement bonus**, gained immediately when you cover them. The left edge holds the 7 player tokens used to support conservation projects (each grants a bonus when taken — always immediately, and some again in each break). The bottom has 5 card slots for your Action cards; the number above each slot is that card's strength. The right side has spaces for partner zoos (5 continents exist, but you can partner with a maximum of 4 — the third requires an upgraded Association action) and universities (3 different ones); fill each column bottom-up and take any bonus printed on a space you cover immediately. Workers, money, and X-tokens live on the notepad.

## Turn Structure

**Taking a turn.** You may not do nothing: playing zero animals or building zero buildings is not a legal action. Use the alternative X-token action when you cannot or do not want to execute a regular action.

 On your turn, choose one of your 5 Action cards, shift it lower than the others to show it is in use, and perform its action with the strength of its card slot (1 = far left through 5 = far right; the further right, the more powerful). After completing the action, remove the card from its slot, shift all Action cards left of the now-empty slot one slot to the right, and place the used card in slot 1.

**X-tokens.** You may use X-tokens to increase an action's strength: each token spent adds +1 strength, then returns to the supply. You may spend any number in one action (for some actions, strength above 5 no longer improves the action). You can never hold more than 5 X-tokens. Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps of that action; resolve its items one at a time. You must pay each item before receiving its own benefits. You set the strength **before** performing the action — X-tokens gained while performing an action cannot boost that same action.

**"After finishing" effects.** If a card effect says "after finishing" your action, complete the action — including moving the Action cards — before executing the effect.

**Upgrading Action cards.** All Action cards start on side I. When you receive a card upgrade, flip one Action card of your choice from side I to side II (it stays in its slot); its improved action is available **from your next action**, while it immediately counts as upgraded for conditions. The current action keeps the strength and kind set at its start; an upgrade gained during it does not add side-II capabilities to it. There are **4 ways to upgrade** an Action card: on the Conservation track, on the Reputation track, and when you gain your second partner zoo or your second partner university. One of them allows you to choose an alternative — so you cannot upgrade all of your Action cards.

**The Break track.** At the start of the game and after each break, the Break token sits on the starting space for your player count. Various actions and card effects advance it toward the end of the track. When it reaches the **last space**, you call a break for everyone: the break takes place after the end of your current turn, and you get **1 X-token** for reaching the last space. Ignore any additional steps beyond the last space. After the break, the token returns to its starting space.

**Break procedure** (all players, in order):
1. **Hand card limit:** discard cards of your choice down to your hand limit — normally 3, or 5 with a particular university.
2. **Tokens on Action cards:** return any Multiplier, Venom, and/or Constriction tokens on your Action cards to the supply; they no longer have any effect.
3. **Association board:** return all your association workers to your notepad (active again — all tasks are again available at 1 worker). **Restock one tile of each partner-zoo continent and each university kind**, except kinds **already owned by every player**; do not add duplicate available tiles.
4. **Replenish display:** discard the two bottom cards of the display (folders 1 and 2), move the remaining cards down, and refill the display.
5. **Take income** (when multiple players take display cards, **refill the display after each player**; usually simultaneous; if effects require an order, begin with the player who initiated the break — or the affected player closest to them — and proceed clockwise):
   - a. Money according to your zoo's **appeal** (the amount printed next to your counter on the Appeal track; e.g., space 7 pays 11 money).
   - b. **Kiosk income:** for each kiosk, take 1 money per unique building, special enclosure, **occupied** standard enclosure, and pavilion adjacent to it (sharing at least one side of a space). An empty standard enclosure provides no income, but an empty special enclosure does.
   - c. All income marked with the break-income icon on your Sponsor cards and on your **activated** zoo-map bonuses (those uncovered by supporting conservation projects).
   **When more than one player receives a display card during break income, resolve those players clockwise starting with the break initiator (or the first affected player clockwise from them). Refill the display after each such player's income before the next affected player chooses.** This ordering and the between-player refill apply together.
6. **Break track:** return the Break token to the starting space for your player count. Play then continues clockwise with the next player.

## Actions

The position of the Action card sets its strength; each card has a stronger side II once upgraded.

### CARDS action
- **Side I:** Advance the Break token **2 spaces** (you do not gain money for this). Then either **draw from the deck** — compare the strength of the slot with the table on the card and draw the indicated number of cards (maximum 3), after which you might have to discard a card from your hand (one just drawn or one already held) — or **snap**: with strength **5 or more**, instead take exactly **1 card of your choice from the display** into your hand, regardless of your reputation. Replenish the display at the end of your turn. There is no in-turn hand limit; you only discard to your limit during breaks.
- **Side II:** Advance the Break token 2 spaces, then draw cards from the deck **and/or from within reputation range** (the display up to your Reputation counter), in any order, using the upgraded table on the card (e.g., at strength 5 you take 4 cards and discard 1). The display is not replenished until your turn is complete. Snapping now works from strength **3** (strength above 3 makes no difference to a snap). **On either side, snapping takes exactly one display card of any reputation, with no deck draw; the reputation restriction applies only to the side-II draw option, not snapping.** Upgrading the Cards action also lets you progress **past 9 reputation** on the Reputation track.

**Reputation spaces and rewards:** reputation begins at 1. Each display folder covers these Reputation-track spaces:

| Display folder | Reputation spaces |
|---|---|
| 1 | 1 |
| 2 | 2–3 |
| 3 | 4–6 |
| 4 | 7–9 |
| 5 | 10–12 |
| 6 | 13–15 |

At reputation 5 upgrade an Action card; at 8 hire a worker; at 11 gain one conservation; at 12 gain one X-token; at 13 take one in-range display card or draw one deck card; at 14 gain one conservation; at 15 gain one X-token. Each track bonus is received immediately once. Reputation 10 still requires Cards II.

**Reputation track and display:** whenever you increase reputation, advance your counter 1 step. Reaching a space with a bonus grants that bonus immediately, once. Reputation 10+ requires the upgraded Cards action (reminder icon on space 10 / folder 5). If your counter is on space 15 and you gain more reputation, it stays on 15 and you take **1 appeal per remaining reputation step**. "Within reputation range" = the display card on the folder matching your counter plus all lower-numbered folders. After a turn in which display cards were taken: move cards from higher-numbered folders down (keeping their order), then fill empty spaces from the deck. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.

### BUILD action

Place a newly built standard enclosure **empty side up** (yellow border and size number). Each placement-bonus icon covered is awarded immediately **once**; resolve all covered bonuses before the next building. A standard enclosure turning occupied later does not award its covered placement bonus again.

**Buildings available through Build:**

| Building | Footprint / cost | Maximum in one zoo | Minimum Build side |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standard enclosure | Size 1–5 / two money per hex | Multiple | I |
| Kiosk or pavilion | Size 1 / two money | Multiple (kiosks obey spacing) | I |
| Petting Zoo | Size 3 / six money | **One** | I |
| Reptile House | Size 5 / ten money | **One** | II |
| Large Bird Aviary | Size 5 / ten money | **One** | II |

The supply has four tiles of each special enclosure for the four players; **each individual zoo may contain only one of each type**.
- **Side I:** Build **exactly 1 building** of your choice, of size up to the action's strength. Pay **2 money per space** (cost = size × 2) into the supply before placing. Available: kiosk (size 1), pavilion (size 1), standard enclosures (sizes 1–5), and the Petting Zoo (special enclosure, size 3; maximum 1 per zoo — other buildings can be built more than once).

"I" means an instant benefit on playing; "R" a recurring trigger or ongoing permission; "B" break income; "F" final scoring. Effects referring to icons count the card itself. ### Base Final Scoring and map clarifications

**Printed scoring tables:** Sponsored Zoo gives 1/2/3/4 conservation for 3/6/8/10 Sponsor cards. Large Animal Zoo gives 1/2/3/4 conservation for 1/2/4/5 large animals (printed standard size 4–5). Use the highest fulfilled tier; the four-point cap still applies.


- **Architectural Zoo (004):** connected means uncovered and beside a covered space. For full coverage count building spaces, excluding water/rock.
- **Conservation Zoo (005):** count project supports by missing left-map tokens.
- **Naturalists' Zoo (006):** empty building spaces include upgrade-restricted spaces even if Build was not upgraded, but exclude water/rock.
- **Biodiverse Zoo (009):** gain **1 conservation per animal category** for which your zoo has more icons than the player to your right, **maximum 4 conservation**. If they have none of a category, one icon of yours is enough to win that category.
- **Map 1, Observation Tower:** its bonus applies only to standard enclosures adjacent to the tower hex itself, not just another rock hex. Housing an animal there gives the two appeal again after an earlier animal was released. Special enclosures get no tower effect. The tower is not a building for kiosk income.
- **Map 2, Outdoor Areas:** a standard enclosure touching the Outdoor Area hex (not merely another water hex) counts as two spaces larger **for all purposes after placement**. This bonus cannot be ignored on release or transfer; a physical size-2 enclosure there is treated as size 4. No effect on special enclosures; the Outdoor Area is not a building.
- **Map 4, Commercial Harbor:** a building on its adjacent building space connects/activates it. Your first building may start beside the Harbor, but need not. Its discard ability may be used before, during or after your action, only once per own turn; never during breaks or another player's turn. The Harbor is not a building.
- **Map 5, Park Restaurant:** break income is one money per adjacent **covered hex**, regardless of building type, occupancy or several hexes belonging to one building. The Restaurant is not a building. Its special-enclosure placement bonus gives **one Reptile House or one Large Bird Aviary** free, even before Build II. Choose one, not both, and follow the other normal placement rules.
- **Map 6, Research Institute:** a building on its adjacent building space activates it; your first building may begin there but need not. Thereafter ignore one Animal-card condition, including one required icon or the Animals upgrade. All other conditions and all terrain requirements remain. The Institute is not a building.
- **Map 7, Ice Cream Parlors:** once all printed **kiosk placement-bonus spaces** are covered, every kiosk gives one extra money each break, whether built free or normally, even with no normally qualifying neighbors.
- **Map 8, Hollywood Hills:** cover H spaces by placing buildings under the ordinary placement rules. When an H is covered, reveal deck cards until a Sponsor appears; keep it and discard the others. H is not a placement bonus (so does not trigger Archaeologist). After covering all three, every Sponsor's level is one lower. Its bonus partner zoos still require Association II for the third/fourth partner; bonus buildings still require Build II to cover upgrade-marked spaces.

### Official base FAQ

**Bonus icons:** an indicated size-2 or size-3 standard-enclosure bonus immediately builds that enclosure once for free, following ordinary placement and map-upgrade restrictions. An ignore-one-condition bonus removes one requirement from a card's left edge; it does not remove terrain requirements. A special-enclosure symbol used as an immediate effect builds that indicated enclosure free. Take icons for money, reputation, conservation, X-tokens and workers in their shown quantities; worker activation follows the reserve order.


- A bonus granting a partner zoo or university takes an **available Association-board tile**, not one directly from general supply. A third/fourth partner requires Association II from any source; upgrade-restricted building spaces require Build II even with free buildings or Sponsors.
- A bonus letting you pay money to play a Sponsor costs money equal to that Sponsor’s level and requires its usual play conditions. Play it **only from hand**, even if Sponsors is upgraded. This paid-Sponsor effect leaves the Sponsors Action card in its current slot; it does not move it.
- A left-side **maximum 25 appeal** condition permits play only while your zoo has at most 25 appeal. The matching marker at appeal 25 is a reminder, not a general track cap. A minimum-reputation condition requires at least its printed reputation value. An Animal partner-zoo condition means a partner from its continent; a Sponsor partner-zoo condition permits any continent.
- Appeal cannot exceed **113**, nor conservation **41**; gains beyond those ends are lost. Reputation has its own overflow rule described above.

**The two end triggers give different final turn sets:** an end triggered at the end of a player's own turn gives every other player one final turn; an end triggered during a break gives every player one final turn. A normal break alone does not give any extra turns.

## Player Reference

- **Your turn:** pick 1 of your 5 Action cards → perform it at its slot's strength (1–5, +1 per X-token spent beforehand) → move it to slot 1, sliding the cards left of its slot one step right.
- **The 5 actions (side I → side II):**
  - **CARDS:** advance Break token 2; draw from deck per table (max 3, maybe discard 1), or snap 1 display card at strength 5+ → also draw within reputation range; snap from strength 3; reputation past 9 unlocked.
  - **BUILD:** 1 building, size ≤ strength, 2 money/space (kiosk, pavilion, standard enclosure, Petting Zoo) → several *different* buildings, total size ≤ strength; adds Reptile House & Large Bird Aviary and the restricted map spaces; full map = +7 appeal.
  - **ANIMALS:** play animals from hand per table (conditions → cost, −3/icon with matching partner zoo → empty enclosure of required size → effects) → also from display (pay folder number); at strength 5+, +1 reputation first.
  - **ASSOCIATION:** exactly 1 task (worker required; strength ≥ task value): +2 reputation / partner zoo / university / conservation project work → multiple different tasks, total value ≤ strength, plus max 1 donation (smallest visible amount, +1 conservation point).
  - **SPONSORS:** play 1 Sponsor card (strength ≥ level) OR advance Break token = strength and take that much money → play multiple (strength +1 ≥ total levels), also from display; break option pays double money.
  - **X-TOKEN (always available):** move a card to slot 1 and take 1 X-token (impossible with 5 X-tokens held).
- **Costs & limits:** buildings cost size × 2 money · max 1 each of Petting Zoo / Reptile House / Large Bird Aviary · kiosks ≥3 spaces apart · max 4 partner zoos (3rd needs upgraded Association) · hand limit 3 (5 with university), checked only at breaks · max 5 X-tokens.
- **Break:** discard to hand limit → clear Multiplier/Venom/Constriction tokens → recall workers, restock zoos/universities → discard display folders 1–2 and refill → income (appeal money + 1 money per building adjacent to each kiosk [occupied standard enclosures, special enclosures, pavilions, unique buildings] + break-income icons) → reset Break token.
- **Upgrades (4, choose wisely):** Conservation track space 2 (or extra worker) · Reputation track · 2nd partner zoo · 2nd university.
- **Game end:** at end of your own turn or during a break, your Appeal and Conservation counters in the same scoring area (or crossed) → finish turn, everyone else gets one more turn (during a break: everyone gets one more turn).
- **Score:** discard a Final Scoring card if no one hit 10 conservation points → score end-game cards and Final Scoring cards (max 4 conservation points each) → **VP = Appeal − lowest Appeal value in your Conservation counter's scoring area**. Highest positive VP wins; ties: most conservation projects supported, then shared victory.
